# Saved main-data AUC overlap audit: V725 and V737

Status: new bounded forensic result awaiting independent whole-argument review. This is not a native-construction theorem or historical assay reproduction. Research parent: `2ab565c3f5bf10305a96ddeef30901de49959ba5`. Prior PR151 source-assessment head: `571c647615f9ea2e77ce4705febf5e1b497cbba9`.

## 1. Premises and provenance

P1. The supplied archival inputs are the original downloaded V725 observable-only source, main CSV and result JSON; and source, main CSV and result JSON extracted byte-for-byte from the original V737 reproducibility ZIP. Their full bytes and identities are included, not only extracted summaries. `SOURCE_IDENTITIES.json` gives SHA256, byte length and Git blob identity. The V725 and V737 source blobs exactly match the immutable PR151 transcriptions. This authenticates the current downloaded source against those transcriptions, not historical runtime, executable environment, execution order, data generation or creation-chain provenance.

P2. Labels, k settings, target access, dynamics, trajectories and all saved scores are SUPPLIED synthetic data. They are not native event typing, owner identity, physical probability, action or receiver access. Actual atemporal measurement/pruning occurrence remains ACCEPTED INPUT. No additional cause-of-occurrence requirement is introduced.

P3. The declared comparison is ordinary exact-tie empirical Mann–Whitney AUC, assigning 1 for a positive score strictly greater than a negative score, 1/2 for exact equality, and 0 for less-than. Label 1 is positive, matching both actual scorers. No sign reversal, score re-estimation, new metric, label selection or parameter tuning is performed. This rule differs from any proposed approximate-tie convention; no approximate-tie convention is silently substituted.

P4. The V725 source uses NumPy `isclose(p, neg)` with defaults rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-8. On the finite values audited here, its predicate is |p-n| <= 1e-8 + 1e-5|n|. The negative score is the reference argument, so the tolerance is asymmetric. NumPy 2.3.5 is pinned for this audit, not asserted to be the historical environment. The full source records its scoring and data-writing scheme; the generator is never imported or executed.

## 2. General comparator identity on finite saved values

For the Cartesian product of positive and negative rows, let N be the number of comparisons, W the strict-greater count, T the exact-equality count and C the isclose count. The actual V725 accumulation is (W+C/2)/N. Exact-tie empirical AUC is (W+T/2)/N. Every finite exact tie is close, so the difference is (C-T)/(2N), nonnegative.

A close unequal win satisfies both predicates and is credited 1.5, while a close unequal loss is credited .5 instead of zero. Therefore both unequal-close wins and unequal-close losses contribute to the excess relative to exact-tie AUC. This identity is a statement about the audited comparator, not a theorem that all datasets are affected, nor a claim that replacing one function validates the scientific model.

## 3. Complete V725 main-row result

The CSV contains 480 rows: exactly one label-0 and one label-1 row for each pair_id in 0..239. Label 0 has k=.9, label 1 k=.25. Every audited score is finite. N=240*240=57600 for every score. All corresponding saved main-summary JSON numbers are exactly reproduced by the original formula.

| Score | W | T | C | Actual saved formula | Exact-tie AUC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| restoration_distance | 57595 | 0 | 0 | 11519/11520 | 11519/11520 |
| adm_z | 57595 | 0 | 0 | 11519/11520 | 11519/11520 |
| g_atrium_observable_only | 57488 | 0 | 0 | 3593/3600 | 3593/3600 |
| g_atrium_with_k_oracle | 57556 | 0 | 0 | 14389/14400 | 14389/14400 |
| passive_mean | 28680 | 240 | 254 | 28807/57600 | 1/2 |
| passive_curvature | 28680 | 240 | 242 | 28801/57600 | 1/2 |

The four active/oracle values are approximately .9999131944444445, .9999131944444445, .9980555555555556 and .9992361111111111. They have no isclose comparisons at all. Thus this overlap does not explain their high AUC on these saved main rows. It does not thereby validate those scores, calibration, dynamics or access assumptions.

Both passive class score multisets match exactly. Passive mean has seven unequal-close wins and seven unequal-close losses; its excess is 14/115200, taking .5001215277777777 to exactly .5. Curvature has one unequal-close win and one unequal-close loss; its excess is 2/115200, taking .5000173611111111 to exactly .5. The historical Markdown reported these passive values to three decimal places as .500, so its main rounded qualitative comparison does not change.

For a concrete affected pair, passive_mean positive pair_id 24 is .5052135036274827 and negative pair_id 65 is .505210800443534. Their difference 2.7031839487934306e-6 is below the isclose tolerance 5.062108004435339e-6. This comparison receives 1.5. The reverse pair, also close here, receives .5. The complete affected comparison records are preserved in exploratory/RESULTS.json. No selection of just this example is used to calculate the result.

## 4. V737 comparison and floating aggregation

The bundled V737 source uses greater-than plus half exact-equality, which are disjoint. The main CSV has 840 rows / 420 complete paired IDs. Its atrium_scalar strict-win count is 169348 of 176400 comparisons, with no exact ties, yielding 42337/44100. The source's NumPy mean-of-row-means aggregation yields .9600226757369613, exactly matching the saved JSON. Direct rational-to-float conversion yields .9600226757369614. That one final aggregation-rounding difference is not an AUC mismatch. Restoration residual is 1, and both passive AUCs are 1/2; the actual scorer reproduces their saved values too.

The exploratory result JSON additionally applies the V725 formula hypothetically to V737 scores as a comparison control. Those values are NOT actual V737 outputs or defects. The audited V737 implementation itself has no V725 predicate-overlap bug.

V737 changes the dynamics, endpoint stencil, noise scaling and metric. Its correct disjoint comparator and internal main-data agreement do not make it an exact V725 replay or authenticate V725 scan/ablation AUCs.

## 5. Evidence method and countercontrols

An initial NumPy vector comparison audit was followed by separate scalar comparison counts and combined-average-rank exact-tie reconstruction. The declared row universe, both labels, complete pairing, finite values and all main scores are checked, not merely a supplied subset. Exact original input hashes are enforced before scoring. Rejecting controls exercise missing, duplicate and substituted rows, incorrect labels, nonfinite values and incorrect summary results. Their evidence is retained separately. Independent review must inspect the actual programs, rows, formulas and calculations rather than treating local agreement as acceptance.

The exploratory audit predates the review freeze and is explicitly not retrospectively preregistered. Subsequent fixed-data verification reproduces this bounded result; it is not a scientific generator run or numerical campaign. Original source and output bytes are preserved unchanged. This audit does not repair the historic source in place.

## 6. Exact limits and next obligation

Only the V725 and V737 main datasets are rescored. V725's saved JSON contains scan/ablation summaries, but the inspected CSV contains only main rows and the output-writing schema does not preserve those other row sets here. Their exact correction cannot be recovered from those summaries alone. V737's ZIP includes a gap CSV, but it is not scored in this task. No missing historical dataset is generated to fill the gap.

The source-and-data linkage is a present-byte hash match plus exact summary reproduction, not proof of historical generation. Prior PR151 Gemini acceptance covered the static caveat and supplied k-to-response trace, not this new data audit. No prior acceptance is imported. The inherited foundational stack and physical model are not recertified. No GR, geometry, physical probability, receiver delivery, certification or native source-event-owner correspondence is derived. Native bridge remains NOT_DERIVED and no premise moves from SUPPLIED to DERIVED.

The numerical next obligation, only if other historical numbers are to be reused, is to locate their exact original row-level outputs and verify the comparator on those inputs rather than extrapolate this result. The native next obligation remains a source-backed event-operation-same-owner available-effect correspondence; these synthetic rows do not provide it. No sweep, replay, metric tuning, new owner label or review of unchanged material is requested.

# Prospective review and publication plan

This bounded saved-data audit follows the user's authorized V725 overlap investigation and independent adversarial whole-argument review/publication workflow. It is not a numbered retained-research stage or a native scientific execution. All numerical findings in ARGUMENT.md and exploratory/RESULTS.json are already known before this freeze; they are not retrospectively preregistered.

1. Freeze original source and saved-main-data bytes, source identities, complete argument, this plan, exploratory evidence and verification code on an isolated branch from verified research head 2ab565c3f5bf10305a96ddeef30901de49959ba5. Preserve current source rights and provenance. Do not modify another research branch or original historical files.
2. Reconstruct all main rows/pairs and AUC comparisons via independent implementation, with missing/duplicate/substituted/invalid-data and incorrect-summary rejecting controls. Execute only bounded fixed-score arithmetic, not historic generators, scans, ablations or model calibration. Pin current numerical dependencies and disclose their distinction from unknown historical versions.
3. Freeze a byte-locked whole-argument packet containing complete sources and main CSVs/results plus argument and verifier. Use the existing exact-model Gemini transport and Actions secret. One generation, adversarial and unanchored by local or previous ACCEPTED verdicts. No fallback or retry generation of unchanged material. Preserve raw response and failed evidence.
4. Read all ordinary raw response text, findings, substantive checks, limits and verdict. Resolve objections without erasing original evidence. Separate publication rechecks immutable remote identities, request/prompt/raw response consistency and fresh deterministic fixed-data verification. Do not infer acceptance from a green upload or local agreement.
5. Preserve original artifact ZIPs, logs, manifests, argument and full evidence in GitHub; immutable full readback before claiming readiness. No merge or CLOSED/CERTIFIED status is authorized. Report exact remaining gates and bounded results to the bot thread. PR130/131 holds and all concurrent work stay unchanged.

Prior PR151 review is context, not acceptance of this new rescore. No scientific generator, native test campaign, inherited-stack recertification, new access assumption, owner assignment or physical promotion is part of this review.

"""
V725 Observable-Only Atrium Metric Extraction

Purpose:
  Reset Step 3 to the correct order after V723:
    passive burden = chance
    active restoration = signal

  This script extracts a first operational Atrium metric scalar from paired,
  passive-equivalent perturbation-response assays.

Boundary:
  This is NOT a GR metric tensor and does NOT derive Einstein equations.
  It is a response-geometry scalar candidate to be tested before V726 invariance.

Run:
  python v725_clean_atrium_metric_extraction.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import numpy as np


EPS = 1e-9


@dataclass
class RunMetrics:
    pair_id: int
    label: int                 # 0 = high restorative capacity, 1 = impaired restorative capacity
    k: float
    restoration_distance: float
    contraction_rate: float
    trajectory_deviation: float
    curvature_second_variation: float
    observation_window_boundary: float
    metric_strain: float
    passive_mean: float
    passive_curvature: float
    adm_z: float = np.nan
    g_atrium_observable_only: float = np.nan
    g_atrium_with_k_oracle: float = np.nan


def auc_score(y_true: np.ndarray, score: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mann-Whitney AUC without sklearn dependency."""
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    score = np.asarray(score).astype(float)
    pos = score[y_true == 1]
    neg = score[y_true == 0]
    if len(pos) == 0 or len(neg) == 0:
        return float("nan")
    wins = 0.0
    total = len(pos) * len(neg)
    for p in pos:
        wins += np.sum(p > neg) + 0.5 * np.sum(np.isclose(p, neg))
    return float(wins / total)


def curvature_like(x: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mean absolute second difference across a 1D retained atlas field."""
    if x.size < 3:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(np.diff(x, n=2))))


def make_target(n: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Smooth target field with mixed low-frequency structure."""
    t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
    target = (
        0.85 * np.sin(t)
        + 0.35 * np.sin(2.7 * t + 0.4)
        + 0.18 * np.cos(5.1 * t - 0.2)
    )
    target += 0.03 * rng.normal(size=n)
    return target


def make_passive_equivalent_state(target: np.ndarray, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """Create same passive burden start for each pair; both arms copy this exactly."""
    n = target.size
    t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
    burden_shape = 0.75 * np.sin(1.3 * t + 1.2) + 0.35 * np.cos(3.9 * t)
    local_roughness = 0.08 * rng.normal(size=n)
    x0 = target + burden_shape + local_roughness
    return x0


def perturb_state(
    x0: np.ndarray,
    mask: np.ndarray,
    amplitude: float,
    direction: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Identical perturbation applied to both paired arms."""
    return x0 + amplitude * mask * direction


def relax_response(
    x_start: np.ndarray,
    target: np.ndarray,
    k: float,
    noise_schedule: np.ndarray,
    steps: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Active restoration dynamics.

    k controls retained restorative capacity. Everything else is shared within each pair.
    The nonlinear flow term adds a weak geometry-dependent response component without
    changing the passive baseline.
    """
    x = x_start.copy()
    path = [x.copy()]
    n = x.size

    for s in range(steps):
        residual = target - x
        lap = np.zeros_like(x)
        lap[1:-1] = x[:-2] - 2 * x[1:-1] + x[2:]
        lap[0] = x[1] - x[0]
        lap[-1] = x[-2] - x[-1]

        # restorative pull + mild smoothing + deterministic paired noise
        dx = k * residual + 0.06 * k * lap + noise_schedule[s]
        # capacity-dependent inefficiency: weaker k leaves more deformation unresolved
        dx += 0.015 * (1.0 - k) * np.tanh(lap)
        x = x + dx
        path.append(x.copy())

    return np.asarray(path)


def compute_metrics(
    pair_id: int,
    label: int,
    k: float,
    x0: np.ndarray,
    x_pert: np.ndarray,
    target: np.ndarray,
    path: np.ndarray,
) -> RunMetrics:
    d0 = float(np.linalg.norm(x_pert - target))
    dT = float(np.linalg.norm(path[-1] - target))
    d_prev = float(np.linalg.norm(path[-2] - target)) if len(path) > 1 else dT

    contraction = (d0 - dT) / (d0 + EPS)

    increments = np.diff(path, axis=0)
    path_length = float(np.sum(np.linalg.norm(increments, axis=1)))
    straight_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(path[-1] - path[0]))
    trajectory_deviation = path_length / (straight_distance + EPS) - 1.0

    second = path[2:] - 2 * path[1:-1] + path[:-2]
    curvature_second_variation = float(np.mean(np.linalg.norm(second, axis=1))) if len(path) > 2 else 0.0

    observation_window_boundary = abs(dT - d_prev) / (d0 + EPS)
    metric_strain = path_length / (d0 - dT + EPS) if d0 > dT else path_length / EPS

    return RunMetrics(
        pair_id=pair_id,
        label=label,
        k=float(k),
        restoration_distance=dT,
        contraction_rate=float(contraction),
        trajectory_deviation=float(trajectory_deviation),
        curvature_second_variation=curvature_second_variation,
        observation_window_boundary=float(observation_window_boundary),
        metric_strain=float(metric_strain),
        passive_mean=float(np.mean(np.abs(x0 - target))),
        passive_curvature=curvature_like(x0 - target),
    )


def zscore_from_admissible(values: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Normalize by high-capacity/admissible arm only."""
    base = values[labels == 0]
    mu = float(np.mean(base))
    sd = float(np.std(base) + EPS)
    return (values - mu) / sd


def normalize01(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    lo = float(np.min(values))
    hi = float(np.max(values))
    return (values - lo) / (hi - lo + EPS)


def finalize_metric(metrics: List[RunMetrics]) -> List[RunMetrics]:
    labels = np.array([m.label for m in metrics])

    restoration = np.array([m.restoration_distance for m in metrics])
    contraction_fail = 1.0 - np.array([m.contraction_rate for m in metrics])
    traj_dev = np.array([m.trajectory_deviation for m in metrics])
    curvature = np.array([m.curvature_second_variation for m in metrics])
    boundary = np.array([m.observation_window_boundary for m in metrics])
    strain = np.log1p(np.array([max(m.metric_strain, 0.0) for m in metrics]))
    retained_capacity_deficit = 1.0 - np.array([m.k for m in metrics])  # oracle/leakage control only

    adm_z = zscore_from_admissible(restoration, labels)

    # Certified candidate: observable-only, no direct k.
    g_observable = (
        adm_z
        + 1.50 * normalize01(contraction_fail)
        + 0.75 * normalize01(traj_dev)
        + 0.75 * normalize01(curvature)
        + 0.50 * normalize01(boundary)
        + 0.25 * normalize01(strain)
    )

    # Oracle/leakage control: direct k is reported but does not count.
    g_oracle = g_observable + 0.50 * normalize01(retained_capacity_deficit)

    for i, m in enumerate(metrics):
        m.adm_z = float(adm_z[i])
        m.g_atrium_observable_only = float(g_observable[i])
        m.g_atrium_with_k_oracle = float(g_oracle[i])
    return metrics


def run_assay(
    k_high: float = 0.90,
    k_low: float = 0.25,
    n_pairs: int = 240,
    n: int = 64,
    steps: int = 32,
    seed: int = 725,
) -> Tuple[List[RunMetrics], Dict[str, float]]:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    metrics: List[RunMetrics] = []

    for pair_id in range(n_pairs):
        target = make_target(n, rng)
        x0 = make_passive_equivalent_state(target, rng)
        mask = (rng.uniform(size=n) < 0.42).astype(float)
        direction = rng.normal(size=n)
        direction = direction / (np.std(direction) + EPS)
        amplitude = rng.uniform(0.35, 0.85)
        x_pert = perturb_state(x0, mask, amplitude, direction)

        # Identical relaxation noise in both arms.
        noise_schedule = 0.0025 * rng.normal(size=(steps, n))

        for label, k in [(0, k_high), (1, k_low)]:
            path = relax_response(x_pert, target, k, noise_schedule, steps)
            metrics.append(compute_metrics(pair_id, label, k, x0, x_pert, target, path))

    metrics = finalize_metric(metrics)

    y = np.array([m.label for m in metrics])
    summary = {
        "n_pairs": n_pairs,
        "k_high": k_high,
        "k_low": k_low,
        "k_gap": k_high - k_low,
        "restoration_distance_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.restoration_distance for m in metrics])),
        "adm_z_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.adm_z for m in metrics])),
        "g_atrium_observable_only_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.g_atrium_observable_only for m in metrics])),
        "g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.g_atrium_with_k_oracle for m in metrics])),
        "passive_mean_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.passive_mean for m in metrics])),
        "passive_curvature_auc": auc_score(y, np.array([m.passive_curvature for m in metrics])),
        "mean_paired_delta_g": float(np.mean([
            metrics[2*i+1].g_atrium_observable_only - metrics[2*i].g_atrium_observable_only for i in range(n_pairs)
        ])),
        "max_abs_paired_delta_passive_mean": float(np.max([
            abs(metrics[2*i+1].passive_mean - metrics[2*i].passive_mean) for i in range(n_pairs)
        ])),
        "max_abs_paired_delta_passive_curvature": float(np.max([
            abs(metrics[2*i+1].passive_curvature - metrics[2*i].passive_curvature) for i in range(n_pairs)
        ])),
    }
    return metrics, summary


def k_gap_ablation() -> List[Dict[str, float]]:
    rows = []
    for gap in [0.80, 0.65, 0.50, 0.30, 0.15, 0.05, 0.00]:
        k_high = 0.90
        k_low = max(0.0, k_high - gap)
        _, summary = run_assay(k_high=k_high, k_low=k_low, n_pairs=160, seed=725 + int(gap * 1000))
        rows.append({
            "k_gap": gap,
            "k_high": k_high,
            "k_low": k_low,
            "g_atrium_observable_only_auc": summary["g_atrium_observable_only_auc"],
            "g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc": summary["g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc"],
            "adm_z_auc": summary["adm_z_auc"],
            "passive_mean_auc": summary["passive_mean_auc"],
        })
    return rows


def monotonic_by_k_scan() -> List[Dict[str, float]]:
    """Unpaired scan to verify metric deformation is ordered by k."""
    rows = []
    for k_low in [0.85, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.30, 0.15, 0.05]:
        _, summary = run_assay(k_high=0.90, k_low=k_low, n_pairs=160, seed=900 + int(k_low * 1000))
        rows.append({
            "k_low": k_low,
            "k_gap": 0.90 - k_low,
            "g_atrium_observable_only_auc": summary["g_atrium_observable_only_auc"],
            "g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc": summary["g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc"],
            "mean_paired_delta_g": summary["mean_paired_delta_g"],
        })
    return rows


def write_outputs(metrics: List[RunMetrics], summary: Dict[str, float], ablation: List[Dict[str, float]], scan: List[Dict[str, float]]) -> None:
    out_dir = Path("/mnt/data")
    json_path = out_dir / "v725_observable_only_atrium_metric_results.json"
    csv_path = out_dir / "v725_observable_only_atrium_metric_paired_metrics.csv"
    md_path = out_dir / "V725_OBSERVABLE_ONLY_ATRIUM_METRIC_EXTRACTION.md"

    payload = {"summary": summary, "k_gap_ablation": ablation, "monotonic_scan": scan}
    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    fields = list(asdict(metrics[0]).keys())
    with csv_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(",".join(fields) + "\n")
        for m in metrics:
            row = asdict(m)
            f.write(",".join(str(row[k]) for k in fields) + "\n")

    ablation_lines = "\n".join(
        f"| {r['k_gap']:.2f} | {r['k_low']:.2f} | {r['g_atrium_observable_only_auc']:.3f} | {r['g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc']:.3f} | {r['adm_z_auc']:.3f} | {r['passive_mean_auc']:.3f} |"
        for r in ablation
    )
    scan_lines = "\n".join(
        f"| {r['k_low']:.2f} | {r['k_gap']:.2f} | {r['g_atrium_observable_only_auc']:.3f} | {r['g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc']:.3f} | {r['mean_paired_delta_g']:.3f} |"
        for r in scan
    )

    md = f"""# V725 Observable-Only Atrium Metric Extraction

## Boundary

This is Step 3 only: extract an operational Atrium metric scalar from V723-style passive-equivalent perturbation-response assays.

It does **not** claim a GR metric tensor, Einstein equations, spacetime curvature, or universality.

## Assay

Each counterfactual pair has:

- same passive baseline,
- same pre-probe state,
- same perturbation mask,
- same perturbation amplitude,
- same relaxation noise schedule,
- same target field,
- same observation window,
- only `k` changes.

V723 result carried forward:

```text
passive burden = chance
active restoration = signal
```

V725 asks:

```text
What response geometry is the restoration signal living in?
```

## Extracted components

For each paired run, the script computes:

1. restoration distance,
2. local/global contraction rate,
3. trajectory deviation,
4. response curvature-like second variation,
5. observation-window boundary term,
6. k-dependent metric deformation as an external validation variable only. Direct k is not included in the certified metric.

## Candidate scalar

```text
g_atrium = adm_z
         + 1.50 * contraction_failure
         + 0.75 * trajectory_deviation
         + 0.75 * curvature_second_variation
         + 0.50 * observation_window_boundary
         + 0.25 * metric_strain
```

Where `adm_z` is the restoration-distance deficit normalized against the high-k admissible arm.

## Main result

```text
restoration_distance AUC: {summary['restoration_distance_auc']:.3f}
adm_z AUC:                {summary['adm_z_auc']:.3f}
g_atrium_observable_only AUC: {summary['g_atrium_observable_only_auc']:.3f}
g_atrium_with_k_oracle AUC:   {summary['g_atrium_with_k_oracle_auc']:.3f}
passive_mean AUC:         {summary['passive_mean_auc']:.3f}
passive_curvature AUC:    {summary['passive_curvature_auc']:.3f}
```

Passive-equivalence checks:

```text
max paired passive mean delta:      {summary['max_abs_paired_delta_passive_mean']:.6g}
max paired passive curvature delta: {summary['max_abs_paired_delta_passive_curvature']:.6g}
mean paired delta g_atrium:         {summary['mean_paired_delta_g']:.3f}
```

## k-gap ablation

| k_gap | k_low | observable-only AUC | k-oracle AUC | adm_z AUC | passive mean AUC |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
{ablation_lines}

## Monotonic deformation scan

| k_low | k_gap | observable-only AUC | k-oracle AUC | mean paired delta g |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
{scan_lines}

## Interpretation

V725 cleanly supports this narrow statement:

"""
V737 Reproduce Atrium Metric

Independent reproducibility harness for the frozen V725/V726 result.

Boundary:
  - no direct k in certified metric
  - no adm_z-only shortcut
  - no GR claim
  - no tensor claim

Run:
  python v737_reproduce_atrium_metric.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations
import json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPS = 1e-9
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "outputs"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def roc_auc(y_true, scores):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true).astype(int)
    scores = np.asarray(scores).astype(float)
    pos = scores[y_true == 1]
    neg = scores[y_true == 0]
    if len(pos) == 0 or len(neg) == 0:
        return float("nan")
    return float(np.mean([(p > neg).mean() + 0.5 * (p == neg).mean() for p in pos]))


def second_var(v):
    return float(np.mean(np.diff(v, n=2) ** 2))


def second_diff(v):
    return np.r_[0.0, np.diff(v, n=2), 0.0]


def make_target(n, rng):
    x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
    y = (
        0.50 * np.sin(1.15 * x + 0.2)
        + 0.24 * np.cos(3.1 * x - 0.4)
        + 0.12 * np.sin(7.4 * x + 0.1)
    )
    return y + rng.normal(0, 0.025, n)


def perturbation(n, fam, rng):
    x = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
    p = np.zeros(n)

    if fam == "gaussian_packet":
        c = rng.uniform(0.2, 0.8)
        w = rng.uniform(0.035, 0.10)
        p = np.exp(-((x - c) ** 2) / (2 * w * w)) * rng.choice([-1, 1])
    elif fam == "sawtooth":
        freq = rng.integers(3, 7)
        p = 2 * ((freq * x + rng.uniform()) % 1) - 1
    elif fam == "double_kink":
        c1, c2 = np.sort(rng.uniform(0.15, 0.85, 2))
        p = np.tanh((x - c1) / 0.025) - np.tanh((x - c2) / 0.025)
    elif fam == "colored_noise":
        raw = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
        kernel = np.exp(-np.linspace(-2, 2, 9) ** 2)
        kernel /= kernel.sum()
        p = np.convolve(raw, kernel, mode="same")
    else:
        p = np.sin(2 * np.pi * (2 * x + rng.uniform())) + 0.25 * rng.normal(0, 1, n)

    p -= p.mean()
    p /= p.std() + EPS
    return p


def simulate(target, pert, k, rng, steps=28):
    state = target + 0.55 * pert
    traj = [state.copy()]
    for _ in range(steps):
        force = -k * 0.20 * (state - target) - k * 0.030 * second_diff(state) - 0.010 * state
        noise = rng.normal(0, 0.007 + 0.005 * (1 - k), len(state))
        state = state + force + noise
        traj.append(state.copy())
    return np.asarray(traj), target + 0.55 * pert


def metrics_for_run(pair_id, label, k, family, target, perturbed, traj):
    initial = traj[0]
    final = traj[-1]
    n = len(target)

    d0 = float(np.linalg.norm(initial - target) / np.sqrt(n))
    dT = float(np.linalg.norm(final - target) / np.sqrt(n))
    restoration_residual = dT / (d0 + EPS)

    path_len = float(np.sum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(traj, axis=0), axis=1)) / np.sqrt(n))
    direct = float(np.linalg.norm(final - initial) / np.sqrt(n))
    trajectory_deviation = np.log1p(max(path_len / (direct + EPS) - 1.0, 0.0))

    c0 = second_var(initial - target)
    cT = second_var(final - target)
    curvature_residual = np.log1p(max(cT / (c0 + EPS), 0.0))

    observation_boundary = float(
        np.mean(np.abs(traj[-5:] - target[None, :]))
        / (np.mean(np.abs(traj[:5] - target[None, :])) + EPS)
    )

    metric_strain = np.log1p(path_len / (max(d0 - dT, 0.0) + EPS))

    atrium_scalar = (
        1.50 * restoration_residual
        + 0.75 * trajectory_deviation
        + 0.75 * curvature_residual
        + 0.50 * observation_boundary
        + 0.25 * metric_strain
    )

    return {
        "pair_id": pair_id,
        "label": label,
        "k": k,
        "family": family,
        "restoration_residual": restoration_residual,
        "trajectory_deviation": trajectory_deviation,
        "curvature_residual": curvature_residual,
        "observation_boundary": observation_boundary,
        "metric_strain": metric_strain,
        "atrium_scalar": atrium_scalar,
        "passive_mean": float(np.mean(perturbed)),
        "passive_curvature": second_var(perturbed),
    }


def build_dataset(k_gap=0.80, n_pairs=360, seed=7370):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    families = ["gaussian_packet", "sawtooth", "double_kink", "colored_noise", "mixed"]
    high_k = 0.82
    low_k = max(0.0, high_k - k_gap)
    rows = []

    for pair_id in range(n_pairs):
        target = make_target(72, rng)
        fam = families[pair_id % len(families)]
        pert = perturbation(72, fam, rng)
        pair_seed = rng.integers(0, 2**32 - 1)

        for label, k in [(0, high_k), (1, low_k)]:
            traj, perturbed = simulate(target, pert, k, np.random.default_rng(pair_seed))
            rows.append(metrics_for_run(pair_id, label, k, fam, target, perturbed, traj))

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def summarize(df):
    y = df["label"].to_numpy()
    return {
        "n": int(len(df)),
        "atrium_auc": roc_auc(y, df["atrium_scalar"]),
        "restoration_residual_auc": roc_auc(y, df["restoration_residual"]),
        "passive_mean_auc": roc_auc(y, df["passive_mean"]),
        "passive_curvature_auc": roc_auc(y, df["passive_curvature"]),
        "mean_atrium_high_k": float(df[df.label == 0]["atrium_scalar"].mean()),
        "mean_atrium_low_k": float(df[df.label == 1]["atrium_scalar"].mean()),
    }


def main():
    main_df = build_dataset(k_gap=0.80, n_pairs=420, seed=7370)
    main_summary = summarize(main_df)

    gap_results = []
    gap_frames = []
    for i, gap in enumerate([0.80, 0.65, 0.50, 0.30, 0.15, 0.05, 0.00]):
        df = build_dataset(k_gap=gap, n_pairs=260, seed=8000 + i)
        sc = summarize(df)
        sc["k_gap"] = gap
        gap_results.append(sc)
        gap_frames.append(df)

    family_results = []
    for fam, sub in main_df.groupby("family"):
        sc = summarize(sub)
        sc["family"] = fam
        family_results.append(sc)

    results = {
        "version": "V737",
        "title": "Independent Atrium Metric Reproducibility Harness",
        "direct_k_in_metric": False,
        "uses_adm_z": False,
        "main": main_summary,
        "gap_results": gap_results,
        "family_results": family_results,
        "pass_conditions": {
            "atrium_auc_high": main_summary["atrium_auc"] > 0.90,
            "passive_controls_chance": abs(main_summary["passive_mean_auc"] - 0.5) < 0.05
            and abs(main_summary["passive_curvature_auc"] - 0.5) < 0.05,
            "null_gap_chance": abs(gap_results[-1]["atrium_auc"] - 0.5) < 0.08,
        },
        "boundary": [
            "No direct k inside metric.",
            "No adm_z-only shortcut.",
            "No GR or tensor claim.",
            "Synthetic reproducibility only."
        ]
    }

    main_df.to_csv(OUT / "v737_main_metrics.csv", index=False)
    pd.concat(gap_frames, ignore_index=True).to_csv(OUT / "v737_gap_metrics.csv", index=False)
    (OUT / "v737_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))

    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
